content.user_title: Organize Long AI Tasks with Planning Files
content.value_statement: Long AI sessions can lose goals, decisions, and progress. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to store plans, findings, and logs in project files.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to create task_plan.md, findings.md, and progress.md.
Provides markdown templates for plans, findings, and progress logs.
Defines update rules for phases, decisions, errors, and test results.
Includes scripts to initialize planning files and check phase completion.
Uses hooks to surface the current plan before edits or shell work.
limitations: It does not manage external project systems or tickets.
It relies on the agent to keep files updated accurately.
Its helper scripts only inspect local markdown status markers.
It adds process overhead for simple tasks.

use_cases.title: Plan Multi-Step Implementation
use_cases.description: Break a coding task into phases, decisions, tests, and delivery steps before work begins.

use_cases.title: Track Research Sessions
use_cases.description: Capture sources, discoveries, and open questions during long investigation tasks.

use_cases.title: Resume Long Agent Work
use_cases.description: Reload goals, current phase, findings, and prior errors after a context reset or break.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a complex task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use planning-with-files for this task. Create task_plan.md, findings.md, and progress.md before beginning.

prompt_templates.title: Maintain Progress
prompt_templates.scenario: Keep planning files current during work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use planning-with-files. After each phase, update the plan status, findings, errors, and test results.

prompt_templates.title: Resume Existing Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Continue after a long gap or context reset.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use planning-with-files to resume this project. Read the planning files, summarize current status, and continue from the next phase.

prompt_templates.title: Manage a Full Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use for research, implementation, verification, and delivery.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use planning-with-files to manage a complex task with research, implementation, verification, and delivery phases. Keep decisions and failed attempts documented.

output_examples.input: Start a feature build that needs research, implementation, and testing.
output_examples.output: A task plan with phases, a findings log for research, and a progress log for actions and tests.

output_examples.input: Resume a project after a long session gap.
output: Summarizes the current phase and completed work.
Continues from the next unfinished step.

output_examples.input: Check whether the task is ready to finish.
output_examples.output: A completion review that compares completed phases with pending or in-progress sections.

best_practices: Create the planning files before starting complex work.
Update findings after research, browser, or visual inspection steps.
Record failed attempts and decisions before changing approach.
anti_patterns: Using this skill for a one-step question.
Creating planning files inside the skill installation directory.
Retrying the same failing action without updating the plan.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for multi-step work, research, feature builds, debugging, or tasks that may span many tool calls.

faq.question: Which files does it create?
faq.answer: It guides creation of task_plan.md, findings.md, and progress.md in the active project directory.

faq.question: Does it replace project management software?
faq.answer: No. It creates local planning files for agent context, not shared tickets or team workflows.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What do the helper scripts do?
faq.answer: They initialize local planning files and check whether task plan phases are marked complete.

faq.question: Is it useful for quick answers?
faq.answer: Usually no. The planning overhead is best for tasks with several phases or many tool calls.
